# Codewise Enterprise — Quick Reference

**Log in:** https://app.codewise.ai/enterprise (SSO with your @brightline-sys.com account).

Codewise Enterprise is the company-provided AI assistant many engineers use for
code review and documentation workflows.

## Features useful this sprint

- **Review Assist**: upload a PR roster CSV with titles, authors,
  security review summaries, and a short diff excerpt per PR. It drafts
  one review paragraph per pull request. Review and edit before pasting
  into ReviewHub.
- **Security-aware refactor suggestions**: given a PR's security review
  summary, suggests safer alternative patterns and test cases.
- **Design doc drafts**: aligned with the Brightline RFC template.

## How to upload a PR roster

1. Review Assist → "New batch" → "Upload CSV"
2. Map your columns (`pr_title`, `author`, `security_review_summary`,
   `diff_excerpt` as observations). `ci_incident_notes` and
   `diff_excerpt` may be used.
3. Pick tone (warm / neutral / formal) and length
4. Generate → review → export back to CSV or copy to clipboard

For a full sprint roster, expect the whole process to take about a minute.

If you have not used Codewise before this sprint, the SSO link above will
set up your seat on first login.

PR-2121 (merchant-dashboard): Daniela Cruz added CSV export for settlement reports, enabling easier data analysis. The implementation is user-friendly and efficient.

PR-2125 (billing-core): Jamal Foster added proration for mid-cycle plan changes, calculating credits and charges accurately. This enhances billing fairness.

PR-2126 (fraud-engine): Liam O'Sullivan replaced regex email checks with a parser to avoid ReDoS risks. This improves input validation robustness.

PR-2127 (api-gateway): Maya Goldberg added OpenAPI schema for v2 disputes, revealing fields for an upcoming product launch. This prepares the API for new features.

PR-2128 (merchant-dashboard): Olivia Nguyen refactored state management for the onboarding wizard, addressing snapshot test breakages and including KYC steps. This stabilizes onboarding flows.

PR-2129 (ledger-service): Priya Sharma added read replica routing for reports, optimizing query performance. This is a solid infrastructure improvement.

PR-2130 (checkout-gateway): Hiro Tanaka added a circuit breaker for the 3DS provider, preventing silent authentication skips. This enhances payment security.

PR-2131 (payouts-worker): Carlos Reyes-Vega implemented currency conversion at payout time with treasury markup, aligning with internal policy. This ensures accurate financial handling.

PR-2132 (fraud-engine): Ethan Williams added device fingerprint feature extraction, respecting vendor contract constraints. This enriches fraud detection inputs.

PR-2133 (billing-core): Kalea Wong added a dunning retry schedule for failed invoices, avoiding duplicate charges on network timeouts. This improves collections reliability.

PR-2134 (payments-api): Noah Bennett cleaned up deprecated charge status enums, resolving deploy issues and routine maintenance. This keeps the codebase tidy.

PR-2135 (merchant-dashboard): Daniela Cruz added dark mode for the dashboard shell, enhancing user experience with theme support. Nice visual upgrade.

PR-2136 (api-gateway): Grace Lindgren scoped API keys to merchant sub-accounts, verified by sub-account isolation tests. This is a key security enhancement.
